2.0.s.en: (1) The miracle of the healing of the paralytic

2.0.0.en: Capernaum was the center that Christ used during His preaching in Galilee, so He would go out from it to the villages and return to it. As for the house referred to, many hold that it was the house of the Apostle Peter. When He entered, the house became crowded, and there was no longer room for anyone. And instead of taking some rest after being away for days, Christ began to teach the crowd inside the house.

2.0.1.en: My Lord ... You knew no rest throughout the journey of Your incarnation, in order to give us rest by Your words, Your teaching and Your redemption ... Teach us also to labor for the sake of others, breaking the prisons of our selfishness, and to seize every opportunity to speak of You with others.

2.1.1.en: "Borne of four": that is, his paralysis covered his whole body.

2.1.2.en: And the four men point to the four Gospels, which carry the sinner (the paralytic) to Christ, or they represent the Church, which, by the intercession of her prayers, carries sinners to repentance.

2.1.3.en: Because of the crowd, and their inability to get through to Christ, they went up onto the roof of the house (which was covered with wooden boards and some branches), and broke it up, that is, they were able to open a place in it, and let down the paralytic with his bed before Christ by means of ropes.

2.2.0.en: Christ marveled at their faith and their striving, with its perseverance and toil, and said to the paralytic: "Son (that is, He restored to him his sonship), thy sins be forgiven thee." Thus He granted him spiritual healing before bodily healing, whereas in the healing of the paralytic at the pool of Bethesda, the Lord granted him bodily healing first, because he was despairing and broken, and had no one (Jn 5:5-9).

2.2.1.en: And this teaches us that God, in His love for us, deals with each of us according to his need.

2.3.0.en: The scribes, the teachers of the Law who were present in the house, condemned Christ for His saying and considered it blasphemy.

2.3.1.en: "Blasphemies": blasphemy is everything that offends God or His Law, for who can forgive sins but God alone? Consequently, the blasphemy here is the claim of divinity.

2.4.0.en: "Perceived in His spirit": that is, He knew by His divinity, being the Searcher of hearts and thoughts, and for this reason He surprised them with His knowledge of what was within them, and asked them: Which is easier, to say to the man, "Thy sins be forgiven thee," or to command him to take up his bed and walk? Christ was not waiting for an answer, but wanted to declare to them that He alone has authority over spiritual healing and bodily healing, by forgiving sins and raising up from a hopeless illness.

2.5.0.en: The forgiveness of sins is a hidden spiritual work that man cannot see, and consequently it is possible to doubt whether they have really been forgiven, or whether this one who forgives is a blasphemous and misleading man, whose claim cannot be proved. For this reason the Lord commanded the paralytic to arise, take up his bed and return to his household, which is the work they thought to be the harder! So Christ, besides the miracle of healing, gave the scribes the practical proof of His authority to forgive.

2.5.1.en: "Immediately he arose": that is, at once, and without help from anyone, and he went out walking, so that all who were in the house and outside it were amazed, and they gave glory to God and to His blessed name, confessing that in all their lives they had never seen or heard the like of this.

2.5.2.en: The sight of the four friends still stands before our eyes, for they are an example of self-giving and sacrificial service for the sake of others.

2.5.3.en: You may not, my friend, have a regular service in the Church. But are you at least careful to carry the members of your household to Christ, or to bring Christ to them through your conversation, your prayer, or your reading of the Holy Bible with them?

2.5.4.en: Be careful, beloved ... for if you do not plant Christ in them, the world will plant its poisons in them.

2.6.s.en: (2) The calling of Matthew and his feast

2.6.0.en: After the miracle, Christ went out of the house, fleeing from the glorification of men, to the sea.

2.6.1.en: And when the crowds followed Him, He continued His work of teaching them. And as He walked along, He met St. Matthew, who, like many of the Jews, bore two names, one of them Levi the son of Alphaeus, and he was sitting at the place of receipt of custom (the collecting of taxes), which he collected harshly from the Jews, and for this reason the tax collectors (publicans) were hated by the whole Jewish people: first, for their harshness; second, because they worked for the benefit of the Romans, the occupiers. While he was sitting, Christ called him, and he responded at once, and left everything he had been doing, and arose and followed Him.

2.6.2.en: How great is Your heart, my God ... You call sinners and tax collectors to enjoy life with You and to serve Your holy name. But the difference is the measure of our readiness to leave what occupies us away from You.

2.6.3.en: Grant us, O God, to set aside for You a time and a place ... and to leave behind us the place where we collect our tolls.

2.7.0.en: In his astonishment, and in his disbelief at the Lord's choosing him, Matthew made a feast in his house and invited to it his friends from among the tax collectors and others, that they might come to know Christ. But the scribes and the Pharisees, who had begun to watch and pursue the Lord and to criticize His actions, did not like this gathering, so they addressed their words to His disciples: How can your Teacher sit with these unclean people?!

2.7.1.en: But the Lord, when He heard this speech, answered them, making clear the following spiritual truths: (1) that Christ is the Physician who heals our spiritual illnesses, our sins, and none other.

2.7.2.en: (2) That God does not hate the sinner, but is ready even to sit with him and speak with him for the purpose of saving his soul. (3) That those who feel their spiritual illnesses are the ones who obtain healing, repentance and forgiveness. But the proud, and those who consider themselves healthy, gain nothing from Christ.

2.8.s.en: (3) Christ's answers to the questions of the Pharisees

2.8.0.en: Spiritual zeal moved the disciples of John, and indignation moved the Pharisees, and both groups kept the Jewish fasts, and they asked Christ, with some reproach or fault-finding, about the reason His disciples did not fast. In the verses that follow (vv. 19-22), He explained His answer with three illustrative examples, which are the parable of the wedding, the parable of the cloth, and the parable of the keeping of wine, and each of them had its own purpose and explanation (see also Mt 9:14-17).

2.9.0.en: The parable of the wedding: Christ did not abolish the idea of fasting, but He made clear that it is a means of being with Him at His wedding. And since He was the Bridegroom in the midst of His disciples during His incarnation, there is no need for fasting while the wedding continues. But when He is taken from them by His ascension, fasting will be required of them.

2.10.0.en: The parable of the cloth: another comparison, by which Christ meant the difference between the fasts of the Law and the literal and outward ordinances of the Jews, "an old garment," that is, an ancient garment, and the spiritual fasts with the "new piece," that is, the new heart; and it is not possible to join the two together, lest "the rent is made worse," since new cloth usually shrinks after washing, and so tears the old cloth and increases its damage.

2.11.0.en: The parable of the keeping of wine: a third parable, meaning that new practices need a new spiritual nature, for one who has lived practicing his fasts outwardly all his life cannot bear or understand the requirements of spiritual fasting.

2.11.1.en: "Bottles": the singular is "bottle" (zikk), and these are skin vessels (waterskins) in which wine or water or any liquid is put. "New wine": that is, the new spiritual practice.

2.11.2.en: "Old bottles": that is, ancient ones, referring to man before the renewal of his nature.

2.11.3.en: "New bottles": that is, the new spiritual nature granted to us by Baptism and the Holy Spirit. Therefore new wine, which increases in volume with the passing of time, is not put into old skins that have already stretched, or else the wine is spilled and the skins are ruined.

2.11.4.en: And symbolically, the three preceding parables may point to the effect of the New Testament upon the Old Testament through the life renewed by the Christian faith.

2.11.5.en: And the conclusion, beloved ... may we examine ourselves with a specific question: how do we fast ... how do we pray? For God wants prayer, fasting and prostration in spirit, and not by force of habit ... for fasting in the Old Testament was a deprivation of the body ... but in the New Testament it is a liberation of the spirit.

2.11.6.en: So have you examined yourself beforehand and answered?!

2.12.0.en: The Pharisees observed a new case against the disciples, for as they were walking through the fields, because of hunger, they plucked ears of wheat to eat their grains. Although the Jewish Law permitted this to any hungry person passing through a field (Lev 19:10), and although eating itself was not forbidden on the Sabbaths, what provoked the Pharisees was the plucking of the ears, for they considered it a work that was not lawful to do on the Sabbath.

2.13.0.en: When the Lord noticed the Pharisees lying in wait for His disciples, He began His words with some rebuke, "Have ye never read?", meaning: are you ignorant of the Scriptures, you who are the proclaimers of knowledge?! And He reminded them of the deed of David and his men in the days of their flight from King Saul, and how they entered the tabernacle of meeting and ate of the showbread, which none but the priests eat, because of their great hunger, and that the Lord did not count that as sin (1 Sam 21:1-6).

2.14.0.en: Here Christ came to the conclusion of the intended teaching ... that when God ordained the Sabbath, the Sabbath was not the goal, but the goal was man's rest on this Sabbath. So which has meaning to God: the day or man? By this Christ wanted to correct the narrow conceptions to which people had become accustomed, so that they practiced customs without understanding God's purpose in them.

2.15.0.en: A bold and clear declaration in which Christ declares of Himself that He is God, the Lord of the Sabbath and the Creator of time ... and the Pharisees did not understand what He meant by that.

2.15.1.en: "The Son of man": an expression that Christ often used of Himself, pointing to His incarnation and becoming man. Chapter 3: the healing of the withered hand, the choosing of the Apostles, the opposition of some

3.0.s.en: (1) The healing of the man with the withered hand

3.0.0.en: The preaching was still in Galilee, and this synagogue was in one of its cities. When the Lord entered, as was His custom, to teach, there was there a man with a paralyzed hand, and St. Luke adds that it was his right hand. Everyone watched Him, especially His enemies, to see whether He would break the law of keeping the Sabbath and heal this man, so that they might bring a complaint against Him for doing the miracle!

3.1.0.en: Christ asked the man to stand forth in the midst, either to stir their feelings of mercy and compassion toward the sick man, or so that the sick man might be in a distinguished place where everyone could clearly see the work of God. "Is it lawful on the sabbath days": Christ knew that His enemies were lying in wait for Him, and so, before healing the man, He asked them a question to put them to shame and to rebuke them for the hardness of their hearts, namely whether it is lawful to do good or to do evil on the Sabbath, and everyone kept silent, for they did not know what to answer.

3.2.0.en: The hardness of heart in their not answering Christ showed their evil, which angered the Lord with a holy anger, so He commanded the man to stretch out his hand, and he stretched it out at once and it was freed from its paralysis. It is noted that Christ's anger was against the sin of hardness of heart, and was free from evil, and was mixed with grief for the sinners, for Christ did not intend by His anger any harm to those with whom He was angry.

3.2.1.en: Instead of becoming angry, try to find solutions, and do not make the problem more complicated and tear people down.

3.3.0.en: "The Herodians": a political group of the Jews belonging to Herod the Great, who sided with the emperor of Rome out of desire for power, and there was great enmity between them and the Pharisees, but they united in enmity against Christ and in getting rid of Him, though the motive of each was different, and what they took counsel about shows the evil that was in their hearts.

3.3.1.en: The right hand always signifies man's strength, but sin turns strength into weakness, and puts all of us into some state of paralysis and stiffness ... So command me, O God, to stretch out my hand and be freed from the fetters of my weakness, so that shame is turned into boasting and weakness into strength and victory in Your holy name.

3.4.s.en: (2) The multitudes follow Him and many are healed

3.4.0.en: Pointing to the growth of Christ's fame because of His teaching and His miracles, St. Mark makes clear that those who followed Christ came from every quarter.

3.4.1.en: "Galilee": the north of the country, where He was preaching.

3.4.2.en: "Judaea": the southern part of the country, whose capital is Jerusalem.

3.4.3.en: "From Jerusalem": that is, the followers were not from the villages of Judea, but the meaning is that the fame of Christ had reached the religious capital.

3.4.4.en: "Idumaea": it lies in the far south of the country, and its name comes from Edom (Esau).

3.4.5.en: "Beyond Jordan": that is, east of the river.

3.4.6.en: "Tyre and Sidon": outside the land of Judea, which means that those who followed Christ were not Jews only, but Gentiles also.

3.4.7.en: And the motives of those who followed Him were many, for some followed Him out of curiosity, or seeking healing, or to hear His teaching, or to know His true identity, or to accuse Him.

3.5.0.en: As the crowding increased, and as the sick were eager to touch Him for healing from their diseases, the Lord asked the disciples to find a small ship (a boat) to wait on Him, so that He might enter it and teach the crowds from it, as He often did.

3.6.0.en: Those afflicted by unclean spirits would submit to Him, and the evil spirits came out crying out from His divine authority. But Christ asked and commanded these spirits not to mention His name, for He does not like the wicked to bear witness to Him.

3.7.s.en: (3) The choosing of the twelve Apostles

3.7.0.en: (See also the commentary on Mt 10:1-4; Lk 6:13).

3.7.1.en: St. Luke makes clear (6:13) that the night before the calling of the disciples was spent by Christ in prayer, to teach us that the choosing of servants is a great responsibility, which should not be undertaken without prayer and seeking God's guidance.

3.7.2.en: "And calleth unto him whom he would": it makes clear that the calling of servants is a divine calling, and not according to a human purpose. And God uses His Church and those who call in her in choosing His servants.

3.7.3.en: "And he ordained twelve": from a large number of His disciples, the Lord chose twelve disciples for the purpose that "they should be with him": that they accompany Him always, and learn from Him and watch, in order to bear witness to the whole world by their preaching. "Power": given directly by Him to heal and to cast out demons, and even to forgive sins, as it is stated in (Jn 20:23).

3.8.0.en: The Lord Jesus changed the names of some of the disciples, as He did in ancient times in changing the names of those He chose, such as Abram and Sarai, who became "Abraham and Sarah" (Gen 17:5, 15). A name has importance in a person's life, since it makes clear his mission in service ... So Simon received the name Peter, that is, the rock in faith, and likewise James the son of Zebedee and John, the Lord gave them the name Boanerges, which is a Syriac word meaning the sons of thunder, for they became strong in the Spirit like the heavenly beings.

3.9.0.en: As for the rest of the disciples and the meanings of their names, they are as follows:

3.9.1.en: "Andrew" (truly a man), and he was a fisherman like his brother Peter.

3.9.2.en: "Philip" (the lamp), born in Bethsaida, and he is different from the deacon Philip in (Acts 6:5).

3.9.3.en: "Bartholomew" (son of the one attached to the water), and he is the same as Nathanael, as was the custom of many of the Jews, who bore two names. "Matthew" (gift), and before his choosing he was also called "Levi."

3.9.4.en: "Thomas" (the depths) or (twin), and he was known for rationality and doubt.

3.9.5.en: "James the son of Alphaeus" (he who follows closely), called the son of Alphaeus to distinguish him from James the son of Zebedee, the elder, and he has another name, "James the Less," and he is the writer of the Epistle of James.

3.9.6.en: "Thaddaeus" (he who guards the heart), and he is the brother of James the Less, and is known also by the two names: Lebbaeus and Judas, not Iscariot.

3.9.7.en: "Simon the Canaanite" (the one who hears), and the title "the Canaanite" means the zealous.

3.9.8.en: "Judas Iscariot": "Judas" means praise and thanksgiving, and "Iscariot" means (a man of Kerioth), which is a village of the villages of Judea.

3.9.9.en: "Which also betrayed him": how strange that God chooses a man, and this man does not remain in the honor that God gave him, but his end is destruction!

3.9.10.en: So let us be careful, my brother, of vain boasting, and do not say that I am chosen of God and assured of salvation ... Yes, God called us by His grace to sonship in Baptism, but we must stand firm and resist the lusts and the love of the world and of money which destroyed this disciple.

3.9.11.en: "And they went into an house": the Holy Bible did not mention whose house it was, though the nearest of the houses is the house of Peter.

3.10.s.en: (4) The blasphemies of the Jews and the answer to them

3.10.0.en: In the house, because of the crowding of people around Christ and the disciples' preoccupation with organizing, there was no opportunity at all for them to taste food. And some of the Lord's relatives came from Nazareth to Capernaum in order to lay hold on Him, for what they had heard about Him was confused, and they thought He was extreme; the nearest of people to Him did not grasp His true identity until after a period of time. And this reminds us of what Christ said, that Satan is able to raise up enemies against a man from his own household (Mt 10:36).

3.11.0.en: As for the scribes, the copyists and teachers of the Scriptures, who came down from Jerusalem, the place of the worship of God, they signify those whose thoughts have descended from the height of heaven to the depths, and they came with a new accusation that Christ works by the power of the prince of the demons, because they could not deny the Lord's miracles and His power and authority over everything. "Beelzebub": one of the titles of Satan, and its meaning is (lord of the flies), and he was one of the greatest gods of the pagan cults, therefore he was called the prince of the demons, and was also called the prince of the unclean spirits who enter some people.

3.12.0.en: In these four verses the idea is one, for the Lord Jesus wanted to prove the falsehood of this accusation by giving examples that simple people understand, so that they would not be confused by the opinions of the priests. "And he said unto them": the impossibility of one demon casting out another, for the demons are all one kingdom and one order, so how could it be divided against itself, or resist one another? So also is the case with the members of one household, for Satan is too clever to be divided against himself, lest his kingdom be ruined and come to an end.

3.13.0.en: Christ continues His speech to make clear to them the untruth of their claim that He is a partner of Satan, for He entered by His infinite power into the kingdom of strong Satan, and bound him outside to free people from his authority; so how then can He be described as using the prince of the demons to cast out demons?!

3.14.0.en: Here the Lord, in His reply to the scribes, moves on to make clear the extent of the evil to which they had come, and the punishment of this evil (see the commentary on Mt 12:31-32), and He told them that any sin or offense God forgives a man through repentance, but their blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, who moves man to repentance, has no forgiveness forever, because they rejected the Spirit of God Himself and refused repentance, and so their fate will be destruction.

3.15.0.en: Of course, the Spirit who supports Christ is the Holy Spirit, as it is written: "The Spirit driveth him into the wilderness" (ch. 1:12), see also (Mt 4:1; Lk 4:1). Therefore, when the scribes claimed that He had an unclean spirit, they rejected God and the act of repentance, and blasphemed against the Holy Spirit, and this is the cause of their destruction (v. 29).

3.16.0.en: The holy Virgin Mary came from Galilee, and with her the sons of the maternal aunt of the Lord Christ according to the flesh, and as is commonly known in the region of the Levant, the sons of a maternal aunt are called brothers (as in Upper Egypt, the sons of a paternal uncle are called brothers), and because the house was crowded with people they could not enter, so they sent word by mouth, through the crowd surrounding Christ, asking to see Him.

3.17.0.en: Christ here moves us from the concept of limited bodily kinship to unlimited spiritual kinship. He of course did not mean to neglect His bodily relatives, He who laid down the commandments, among them the two commandments that are repeated often in both Testaments of the Bible: "Honour thy father and thy mother" (from Ex 20:12 to Eph 6:2), and "Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself" (from Lev 19:18 to Jas 2:8), and He is also the One who entrusted the beloved John with the care of His mother the Virgin at the time of His crucifixion. But the intended meaning is that obedience to God and His commandments creates a spiritual kinship that surpasses the kinship of the flesh among the members of one Church, and makes us the true relatives of God ... And St. John Chrysostom adds to this, saying: "A man becomes a mother to Jesus by preaching Him, for he is like one who begets the Lord in the hearts of his hearers."

3.17.1.en: What grace You have given me, my God, that You point with Your hand and say of me "Behold my brethren" ... so grant me always to sit at Your feet like those who sat on that day, to learn and grow in the knowledge of You, and to strive with all my strength to fulfill Your will, and to live by Your commandment, that I may become worthy of what You have called me...

3.17.2.en: The parable of the sower and the mustard seed, the raging of the sea
